findings.title: Hard runtime eligibility removes ordinary game and interactive-3D creation requests
findings.cause: Closed runtime-purpose vocabulary omits ordinary controls/input/feedback work, and creation arm permits only 0..3 words before game/playable. A false eligibility result removes the owner rather than merely adjusting rank.
findings.observed: Implement game controls: baseline rank1 -> absent. Build an accessible cooperative puzzle game: rank1 -> absent. Parent Three.js flame: rank4 -> absent. Same losses with live metadata; need specialist does not restore admission. Later matched parent metadata camera-authoring query: baseline code rank1 -> candidate absent; frozen original metadata lacks Arcadia under both versions. Muse remains candidate rank4. See camera-results.json for the separate bound metadata snapshot.
findings.repairAcceptance: Retain genuine game/runtime and interactive-creation candidates without requiring magic nouns or losing them when useful modifiers are added. Preserve refused/quoted clause exclusions, matching-metadata dispatch, exact IDs, host no-need and existing unrelated-owner controls. Use mechanism-level admission tests, not an exact-query allowlist.

findings.title: Asset nouns satisfy both context and purpose, admitting a false runtime-intent reason
findings.cause: mesh, meshes, textures and gpu appear in both runtimeContext and runtimePurpose, so one object noun satisfies the two stated evidence gates.
findings.observed: Audit the license for this 3D mesh: Arcadia rank1 baseline and candidate; candidate now adds game or real-time 3D runtime scope reason. Texture attribution remains rank2. This is an unclosed promised boundary and new misleading corroboration, not a baseline rank regression.
findings.repairAcceptance: Require evidence of the requested runtime operation/player outcome distinct from the object being discussed; license-only and attribution-only requests must not acquire that runtime-intent reason/admission. Preserve actual mesh integration and mixed requests with a separate live runtime clause.

nonblockingObservations: All 93 bare exact-ID queries remain rank1; natural-language requests containing an ID can lose it under the gate, but inspect's exact-ID API is unaffected.
Topic-only game punctuation and multiword shorthand lose recall; those finite-format limits are separately documented and are not counted as additional blockers.
Cross-sentence runtime pronoun challenge Q11 loses the owner; explicit same-clause game context restores it, consistent with documented discourse limits.
Parent WebGL portal yields no candidates in both baseline and candidate: preexisting lexical coverage gap, not caused by this change. Muse is absent from top20 for both parent prompts.
No fresh regressions observed in the eight non-game task probes or the tested recognized quote/refusal/live-work and host-no-need boundaries.
